tagline.text: A small island off Santa Fe, Bantayan, with white sand and cliff jumping

location.label: Location
location.text: Sea east of Santa Fe, Bantayan Island, Cebu (about 30 minutes by boat from Kota Beach, also called Sillon Island)

duration.label: Time needed
duration.text: Half day (about 3 hours on the island)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱500~1,500 (per person, boat, entrance and gear when 4–8 people share the boat)

children.text: Virgin Island is a small island off Santa Fe on Bantayan Island, with white sand, clear water, a bamboo jumping platform and a coastal boardwalk, and it is a leading destination on half-day island tours. It is privately owned and charges an entrance fee, so confirm prices locally.

Virgin Island is a small island in the sea east of Santa Fe on Bantayan Island. It is also called Sillon (or Silion) Island, and map services list the same place separately as "Virgin Island Resort" or "Silion Island." It takes about
30 minutes

by bangka from Kota Beach in Santa Fe, and the same boat tour often also visits Balidbid Lagoon or the neighboring Hilantagaan Island. The island has white sand, coconut palms, clear turquoise water, a wooden coastal boardwalk and a bamboo jumping platform, and it is a good place to spend half a day.

The island is privately run rather than a public beach, and it charges an entrance fee. A 2010 GMA News visit described only three small caretaker houses and a few huts and said the island was hardly developed. By contrast, reviews from 2018 onward and a guide updated in January 2026 mention cottages, lounge chairs, a beach bar, small restaurants and shops, a boardwalk, kayaks, beach volleyball and cliff jumping, so the facilities have grown a great deal. Rather than expecting the mood of old reviews, check recent reviews.

The routine is simple. Hire a bangka through your lodging's front desk or a tour desk in Santa Fe, pay the island entrance fee, stay a few hours and return to Kota Beach. Guides say they stayed about 3 hours, and beach lovers could stay all day. Boat fares and entrance fees differ greatly between guides, so see the cost table below and negotiate on the spot. The 2010 GMA visit took a bus of about 2 hours 30 minutes from Cebu City and a ferry of about 1 hour 30 minutes, then a tricycle to the pier on Bantayan and about 30 minutes in an eight-seat fishing boat. The route is still the same, so it is better to stay a night in Santa Fe than to make a round trip from Cebu City in one day.

One reviewer noted that no sign on the island explains what "Virgin" means. It is taken to mean a clean, little-developed island, but its exact origin is not known. A map service aggregates about 600 Google reviews with an average of 4.6, which makes it one of the best-loved stops on Bantayan island tours. Some visitors complain that the entrance fee is higher than at other islands because the island is privately owned.

The sand around the island is fine and fairly white, and in shallow water the sea looks clear turquoise. Reviewers say there are coral patches in front of the beach where you can see fish up close. The beach at the back is wider and quieter.

blocks.title: Cliff jumping and the bamboo platform

children.text: At the north end of the island there is a bamboo platform with levels at about
3m
5m
and
8m
, according to guides. Sea depth and currents change from time to time, so ask a lifeguard or your boatman before you jump. If you are new to it, start at the lowest level.
You can snorkel on the reef around the island, and guides mention bamboo ladders that let you enter the sea directly from the boardwalk. Gear is said to rent for about
on the island, but bringing your own is better. The 2010 GMA visit reported currents strong enough to tire swimmers, so wear a life vest.
A wooden boardwalk runs along the island's coast and lets you walk while looking over the main beach. It is a good spot for photos, and since the sun is strong at midday, rest in the shade.

Under the palms there are shaded huts and hammocks. One guide wrote that the entrance fee and a cottage came to ₱350 together, while another said cottage rates depend on size and advised asking beforehand. When you arrive, check the rate first before settling in.

Kayak rental and beach volleyball facilities are said to be available. A beach bar, small restaurants and shops sell drinks and food, but prices on the island are said to be higher than on the mainland, so it is better to bring snacks. On windy days or when the current is strong, do not paddle far from shore.
Guides mention a quiet white-sand beach on the north coast with few people. It gets crowded on weekends, so a weekday morning is much calmer.

blocks.title: Where boats land and lessons from reviews

children.text: A 2018 review says boats dock at the sandbar at the back of the island, where the writer did not swim. That group brought only bread and bananas and left early because they were hungry, so bring a proper meal. In the 2010 visit, lunch was barbecued chicken and puso (rice cooked in banana leaves) with coconut water from the palms. The facilities have since grown, so check locally whether the restaurants are open.
Find a bangka at your lodging or Kota Beach and agree on the price. Sharing among 4–8 people lowers the cost.
Leave Kota Beach and arrive at Virgin Island after about
30 minutes
. Pay the entrance fee and check the cottage rate.
Walk the beaches and boardwalk around the island and look at the jumping platform.
Snorkel or swim. Wear a life vest and watch the current.
Rest in a hammock and have a snack.
Return to Kota Beach at the time you agreed with the boatman.
Agree on the boat's waiting time and return time before you leave.

items.title: From Cebu to Hagnaya and Santa Fe

children.text: Take a bus bound for Hagnaya from the Cebu north bus terminal, which takes about
2 hours 30 minutes to 4 hours
, then board the ferry to Santa Fe. The ferry takes about
1 hour to 1 hour 30 minutes
Fares differ between guides and are revised from time to time, so check the latest at the terminal. One guide mentions a terminal fee and an environmental fee of about
each at Santa Fe port.

items.title: From Santa Fe to Kota Beach

children.text: From Santa Fe port, go to Kota Beach and the beach resort area by tricycle or motorbike. Lodging around Kota Beach is within walking distance.

items.title: By boat from Kota Beach to the island

children.text: Find a bangka at Kota Beach or through your lodging's front desk. It takes about
30 minutes
one way.
Boat fares are about
for the whole boat depending on the guide, and the entrance fee is separate.
One guide says the Kota Beach sandbar appears only at low tide. Check the tide for boat trips and beach use.
The best time is the dry season of
December–May
, when the sea is calm and the sky is clear. Boat rides are easy, and the clear water suits snorkeling. Weekends bring more visitors and crowds, so a weekday morning is quieter.
June–November
is the rainy season, and in
September–November
typhoons can stop boats. Island tours are canceled on windy days, so leave spare days.

The tide also affects your day. One island tour guide says high tide is good for enjoying the beach, and the Kota Beach sandbar appears only at low tide. Decide the best time with your boatman after checking that day's tide.

There are rooms on Virgin Island, and one review says the entrance fee is included in the room rate for overnight guests. Most travelers, however, stay at resorts or guesthouses on the Santa Fe beaches and visit as a day trip. Lodging is full during Holy Week and holidays, so book ahead.

The island has small restaurants, a coffee shop and shops where you can buy drinks and simple meals. Prices are higher than on the mainland, so many guides advise buying snacks and water at a Santa Fe supermarket. One review says bringing your own food is allowed, so confirm at the entrance. Another review says eating your own food in the cottage provided was permitted, so bring a mat and a trash bag and take your trash back with you.
Entrance fees and boat fares differ greatly between guides. When you arrive, check the entrance fee and cottage rate first.
Going on a weekday morning instead of a weekend is much quieter.
Many reviews describe staying on the island for about 3 hours. If you love beaches, agree on the time with your boatman beforehand.
Bring your own snorkeling gear and life vest if possible. Rentals on the island are limited.
When you go up the jumping platform, check the sea depth and current, and start at a lower level the first time.
Buying snacks and water at a Santa Fe supermarket is cheaper and more convenient.
Bring a waterproof bag, sunscreen and a hat.
Boats and cottages run short during Holy Week (late March to mid-April) and holidays. At those times ask your lodging the day before.
If you agree on the order of stops (the island first, the lagoon later, and so on) and the return time with your boatman at departure, you will have fewer disputes on site.
If you get the boatman's contact from your lodging's front desk, bargaining and adjusting the schedule becomes easier.

Because the island is privately owned, fees differ between sources and include old figures. Agree clearly on the boat and entrance fee before departure, and since some reviews mention unexpected docking fees, keep receipts.
Guides say the platform goes up to about 8 m, so there is a risk of accidents. Follow the lifeguard's instructions and do not jump after drinking.
On days with strong currents, swimmers tire easily. Wear a life vest.
One review says the restrooms are not very clean.
Boats may be canceled during the rainy season and typhoon months.
Do not step on or touch the coral.
Because the island is privately owned, its entry rules and fees can change without notice. Ask your lodging for the latest before you leave.
